title: Ripudaman Singh Malik’s Killer Gets 15 More Years for Separate Abbotsford Manslaughter
excerpt: Tanner Fox, already serving life for the assassination of the former Air India bombing suspect, pleaded guilty to the 2022 killing of Chad Colivas in an unrelated break-in gone wrong.
body:
• Tanner Fox, 25, already serving life for the contract killing of former Air India bombing suspect Ripudaman Singh Malik, has been sentenced to an additional 15 years for the manslaughter of Chad Colivas in Abbotsford, British Columbia.
  • Colivas, 41, was shot dead at his home on March 21, 2022, after he confronted Fox, who had entered the property unlawfully. Police say the killing was unrelated to gang activity.
  • Fox pleaded guilty to manslaughter with a firearm in April 2026. An accomplice, Laetitia Acera, received four years plus two years of probation for break and enter.
  • Authorities have never publicly identified who hired Fox and accomplice Jose Lopez to assassinate Malik in 2022. The victim’s family continues to demand answers.

A man already serving life in prison for the assassination of former Air India bombing suspect Ripudaman Singh Malik has been handed an additional 15-year sentence for a separate killing in British Columbia, according to the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team.

Tanner Fox, 25, was sentenced after pleading guilty to manslaughter with a firearm in the death of 41-year-old Chad Colivas of Abbotsford. The sentence, handed down this week, adds to Fox’s existing life term but does not change the parole ineligibility period tied to his murder conviction in the Malik case.

The Colivas Killing

Police found Colivas suffering from gunshot wounds at his home on March 21, 2022. He later died from his injuries.

https://x.com/TheDailyPioneer/status/2080941122373959843

IHIT spokeswoman Freda Fong said Colivas was unarmed when he confronted Fox, who had entered the home unlawfully. Investigators determined the incident had no connection to gang activity.

Fox pleaded guilty to the manslaughter charge in April 2026. A second person arrested in connection with the case, 30-year-old Laetitia Acera, pleaded guilty to break and enter and received a four-year prison sentence followed by two years of probation.

The Malik Assassination

The Colivas case is entirely separate from the crime that first brought Fox to national attention: the contract killing of Ripudaman Singh Malik.

On July 14, 2022 — less than four months after Colivas’s death — Malik was shot dead while sitting in his Tesla outside his family business in Surrey, British Columbia. Fox and accomplice Jose Lopez were arrested within two weeks and later pleaded guilty to second-degree murder.

“I know nothing I say will bring him back and I’m sorry for the role I played in this crime. Not a day goes by that I don’t feel remorse for my actions.”

— Tanner Fox, at his sentencing for the Malik murder

In January 2025, Fox was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole for 20 years. During the proceedings, he told the court he was “young and dumb” when he carried out the killing. His lawyer revealed Fox had been adopted from Thailand by Canadian parents at age three.

Air India Bombing: The Shadow That Never Lifted

Malik’s death drew intense scrutiny because of his ties to one of the deadliest acts of terrorism in aviation history. In 1985, a bomb destroyed Air India Flight 182 over the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Ireland, killing all 329 people aboard. A second device exploded at Tokyo’s Narita Airport, killing two baggage handlers. The attacks, attributed to Sikh separatists, remain the worst mass killing in Canadian history.

Malik and co-accused Ajaib Singh Bagri were acquitted of mass murder and conspiracy charges in 2005 after a British Columbia Supreme Court judge ruled testimony against them was not credible. Despite the acquittal, the case defined much of Malik’s public identity for the remainder of his life.

He went on to lead the Khalsa Credit Union in Vancouver, which grew to more than 16,000 members, and established several schools in the Surrey and Vancouver areas.

Who Ordered the Hit?

Both Fox and Lopez admitted in court that they were “hired and paid” to kill Malik, but neither has revealed who arranged the contract. Prosecutors confirmed the murder was premeditated and financially motivated, yet the identity of the person or persons behind it remains unknown.

Malik’s son, Jaspreet Singh Malik, has publicly pleaded with both men to come forward. “The only question that remains now is who hired Mr. Fox and Mr. Lopez,” he said outside the courthouse after Fox’s sentencing. “I’m asking both Mr. Fox and Mr. Lopez to do the right thing. Tell the RCMP who hired you.”

In October 2024, RCMP Commissioner Mike Duheme said the force had launched a special unit to investigate multiple cases of extortion, coercion, and violence — including murders — linked to agents of the Indian government. Whether Malik’s killing falls within the scope of that investigation has not been confirmed.

What’s Next

Fox’s 15-year sentence for the Colivas manslaughter runs alongside his life sentence. Lopez’s sentencing in the Malik case was completed separately. The IHIT has emphasized that the two investigations remain independent, but Fox’s involvement in both killings — occurring within months of each other in 2022 — underscores a pattern of violence that began when he was barely in his twenties.

For the Malik family, the legal proceedings have delivered accountability for the triggermen but left the central question unanswered: who wanted Ripudaman Singh Malik dead, and why?

nri_angle: The 1985 Air India bombing and Malik’s subsequent acquittal remain pivotal events for the Indian and Sikh diaspora in Canada, and the unresolved question of who ordered his assassination continues to unsettle communities.
